decisions.reason: With a prescribed singleton bin set and two occupied deterministic feature types having probabilities 0 and 1, the common score is constant and cannot equal both outcomes. The original existence clause omitted the freedom to choose bins. The repair preserves the KMR feature-instance convention, explicitly allows choosing bins and scores for this existence question, supplies the deterministic construction, and states the fixed-bin capacity caveat.

The supplier allows rho_t=0 and rho_t=1; only this balance definition imposes 0<mu_t<N_t. Its displayed conditional means already have positive denominators, so the mathematical definition is sound. Corrected only Definition references to attribute nondegeneracy to this item rather than its supplier.

reviews.reason: The joint probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one by the two finite normalizations. Bin calibration includes zero-mass bins; full binary reliability gives exactly the sum over equal-score bins, agreeing with def-probability-calibration. The corrected existence convention follows KMR section 1.1 (bins belong to the assignment), and its section 1.2 construction uses scores 0 and 1. Occupied deterministic types are assigned to their outcome bins; unused feature rows may use any available bin. One occupied outcome needs one bin, and two outcomes require two distinct scores and hence at least two bins. No choice axiom or new supplier is needed. Both owning pages have empty bodies and compact-v1 metadata; no diagram is present or needed.

Under the finite common-assignment law, summing a_tsigma p_sigma X_sigmab v_b gives E_t[S 1_{Y=1}], and division by rho_t gives the positive conditional mean; the complementary formula divides by 1-rho_t. The explicit hypothesis 0<mu_t<N_t with N_t>0 makes both denominators positive. Equality of the respective conditional means is precisely KMR section 1.1 balance, without any assertion of threshold-rate equality. The repaired reference correctly locates this hypothesis here. The supplier repair affects only perfect-prediction existence and leaves every formula used here unchanged. The Definition section is byte-identical, so this reference-only repair causes no new consumer event. No diagram is present or needed.
